$Comment: What a player sees and hears when one tier of a gear set comes on or goes off for them: the
recompute after an equip change found the tier's minimums newly met, or newly unmet. It fires
only for a real change; logging in wearing a full set is a hydrate and says nothing. A piece
going on without a tier changing is Gear_Set_Piece's quiet line instead.
This is the library's own neutral default, so a bare server gets a notice out of the box. A
mod that ships a file with this same name in its own pack replaces it (a pack that lists this
library as a dependency loads after it), and a server owner can do the same from the owner
layer. Override the whole file rather than editing this one.
The moment carries 'set' (the set id, also under 'source' so a merging notice keeps one line
per set), 'name' (what the set is called, already in the reader's language), 'pieces' (how
many distinct members the player has on, never more than 'total'), 'total' (how many pieces
the full set takes, read from its tiers: a set listing two helms and two shields for one helm
and one shield counts to 2), 'desc' (the tier's own line, in the reader's language; absent
when the tier authors no Text), 'next' (the line of the first tier the player has still to
earn, in the reader's language; absent when every tier holds or that tier authors no Text),
'hasnext' (true when 'next' is there) and 'active' (true when the tier came on, false when it
went off). 'player' is always the name of who wears it.
Key is a line from a .lang file; Args names which of those values fill its blanks, in order.
Sound is any SoundEvent id, played at the player's own position, and its Volume a share of that
sound's own loudness (1 as the sound authors it). A bonus comes on whenever a player gears back
up, so it gets the game's soft memory chime at half its volume, never a fanfare. Delete either
group in your override to drop that half; add a Broadcast group to tell the whole server. Tone
colours the whole notification: gold Reward for a bonus coming on, plain Info for one going off, which is
what the first Variants entry says for the 'active: false' case. The second entry is a tier
coming on with another still ahead: its smaller line names this tier's bonus and the next one,
so a player learns what the set holds next without opening a page.
